# APIbase — Universal API Hub for AI Agents
# https://apibase.pro

> One MCP + REST endpoint to 1379 tools from 399 providers. No signup, no subscription, no API key to start — pay per call in USDC (x402 on Base or MPP on Tempo).

Why this endpoint instead of individual providers, and how discover/evaluate/pay/execute
actually work: https://apibase.pro/why (Markdown: https://apibase.pro/why.md). Answers for
specific needs (flight search, image generation, company research):
https://apibase.pro/flight-search-intent, https://apibase.pro/image-generation-intent,
https://apibase.pro/company-research-intent.
Concept pages, in Markdown: https://apibase.pro/x402-vs-mpp.md,
https://apibase.pro/what-is-an-mcp-gateway.md, https://apibase.pro/faq.md.
Full text of every linked Markdown page in one file: https://apibase.pro/llms-full.txt.

## Quick Start for Agents
- Connect: POST https://apibase.pro/mcp (MCP Streamable HTTP)
- Discover tools: call the apibase.discover tool (mcpName apibase.discovery.search) with
  intent/category/max_price_usd — free ($0), ranked by relevance then quality then price,
  returns pricing/payment rails/availability/quality per match (ZZ-03-05)
- Discover tools (REST, no auth): GET https://apibase.pro/api/v1/discover?intent=&category=&max_price_usd=&limit=
- Full catalog: GET https://apibase.pro/api/v1/tools (1379 healthy tools; degraded ones are listed with status; JSON schemas)
- OpenAPI spec: GET https://apibase.pro/.well-known/openapi.json

## Progressive Disclosure
1379 tools across 25 categories (TOOL_DEFINITIONS[].category — the single source of truth
shared by MCP apibase.discover, the REST ?category= filter, and this file, ZZ-03-01). Call
apibase.discover (or GET /api/v1/discover) to find relevant tools:
- No args → best/most-relevant matches across the whole catalog
- category="finance" → finance tools only
- intent="search flights" → aviasales, sabre tools ranked by relevance
All tools remain callable via tools/call regardless of discovery. The discover_tools prompt
still works (kept for backward compatibility) — it now renders apibase.discover's own JSON.
/.well-known/site-facts.json — machine-readable facts the pages are checked against.

## Categories (25)
business, crypto, developer, device, education, entertainment, finance, health,
infrastructure, jobs, legal, location, logistics, marketing, media, messaging, music,
news, podcasts, search, social, space, travel, weather, world

## Payment
- Protocol: x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) or MPP (Authorization: Payment, or Payment-Authorization: Payment next to a Bearer key)
- x402 over MCP: X-Payment header OR params._meta["x402/payment"] (x402 MCP transport v2); the 402 tool result carries the payment requirements in _meta
- Dedup window (x402): an identical repeated lookup of a cacheable tool by the same wallet within 2 minutes is answered from cache and not charged; the response carries X-APIbase-Charged: false and the original receipt. Not applied to MPP, balance or shop.* tools
- Token: USDC on Base mainnet (x402) or Tempo (MPP)
- Prices: $0.0005–$29.99 per call (p90 $0.003)
- Details: https://apibase.pro/.well-known/x402-payment.json
- Receipts: https://apibase.pro/r/<receipt_id>.json, a public immutable receipt for each on-chain billed call
- Payment identifier / idempotency: https://apibase.pro/integrator/agent-guide, persist the intent before you send; re-send the same id, never re-sign
- Tool manifest: https://apibase.pro/api/v1/tools/manifest, definition_sha256 per tool to detect changed definitions
- IMPORTANT: use ONE protocol per request, not both
- If using mppx SDK: set polyfill: false to avoid intercepting x402 requests
- MPP client: mppx >= 0.6.16 (0.4 clients are not supported); the challenge lists one currency, USDC.e on Tempo mainnet (pathUSD on the testnet)
- A replayed MPP credential gets 403 credential_replayed
- Integrator (AI payment for merchants, https://apibase.pro/integrator): Integrator: 0% (pilot) fee from the merchant, min $0.05, orders from $1.00; on Tempo inside the transaction, on Base inside the transaction for clients that support fee-split and invoiced otherwise. Merchants connected: 7.

## Agent Integration Guide
1. Match price to wallet — fetch only tools you can afford:
     GET /api/v1/tools?max_price=0.01     # only tools ≤ $0.01
     GET /api/v1/tools?tier=micro         # < $0.01
     GET /api/v1/tools?tier=standard      # $0.01–$0.99
     GET /api/v1/tools?tier=premium       # <!--tiers:premium-->$1+ (3 tools)<!--/tiers-->
2. Each tool entry includes:
     pricing.price_usd       — sticker price per call
     pricing.cache_hit_price_usd — balance tier only; balances are credited by refunds
       only. Paying via x402/MPP per call is always billed price_usd, cache hit or not.
     tier                    — micro | standard | premium
     min_balance_usd         — minimum on-chain USDC the wallet should hold
     input_schema            — JSON Schema for the call's body
3. 402 challenge body always includes price_usd + min_balance_usd, so you can
   short-circuit signing if your balance is insufficient.
4. Use input_schema to build valid params — avoids 400 schema validation errors.
5. Cache the tool list — it changes only on provider onboards (rare).

<!-- source: https://apibase.pro/why.md -->

# Why APIbase

> One MCP + REST endpoint to APIbase's live tool catalog (counts: <https://apibase.pro/llms.txt>).
> No signup, no subscription, no API key to start — pay per call in USDC (x402 on Base or MPP on Tempo).

An agent that needs an external capability goes through the same four steps regardless of
which provider ends up serving the call: **discover** that a tool exists, **evaluate**
whether it fits (price, schema, availability), **pay** for it, and **execute** the call.
APIbase is built around making all four steps happen against one endpoint instead of one
per provider.

## 1. DISCOVER

Call the `apibase.discover` MCP tool, or `GET /api/v1/discover?intent=...` over plain REST —
both free ($0), no authentication required.

```
GET https://apibase.pro/api/v1/discover?intent=search+flights&max_price_usd=0.01
```

Discovery ranks by relevance, then quality, then price, and returns each match's pricing,
payment rails, availability, and quality signal in the same response. The full catalog is
also fetchable directly at <https://apibase.pro/api/v1/tools> for agents that prefer to
cache it and search client-side.

## 2. EVALUATE

Every tool entry carries what's needed to decide whether to call it, before spending
anything:

- `pricing.price_usd` — the sticker price for that specific call
- `tier` — micro / standard / premium, so an agent can filter by wallet size
- `input_schema` — JSON Schema for the call body, validated before sending
- `min_balance_usd` — the balance a wallet should hold before attempting the call

This is the same JSON the live server returns to any HTTP client — checkable directly at
<https://apibase.pro/api/v1/tools>, not a claim that has to be taken on trust.

## 3. PAY

A priced tool call without a payment header gets back an HTTP 402 challenge naming the
exact price and rail options. Two independent rails are accepted on the same endpoints:

| Rail | Network / asset | Header |
|---|---|---|
| x402 | USDC on Base mainnet | `X-PAYMENT` |
| MPP | USDC.e on Tempo mainnet | `Authorization: Payment` |

Neither rail requires a prior signup step — a correctly signed first payment is enough to
create agent credentials. Full mechanics: <https://apibase.pro/connect>.

## 4. EXECUTE

`tools/call` (MCP) or the equivalent REST call runs the request against the upstream
provider. Payment is escrow-first and the call is idempotent by design; x402: not settled on failure; MPP: refund owed, paid by the operator
([details](/pricing#refunds)). <!-- refund-truth: re-word when REFUND-WALLET-1026 lands -->

## How this compares by class

Comparing by class, not by name:

| Class | What you connect to | Before the first paid call |
|---|---|---|
| Single MCP server | One provider's own tools | Usually nothing for that one provider — but it's still only that one provider |
| MCP marketplace / registry | A directory listing of other people's MCP servers | You still connect to, and often authenticate against, each listed server separately |
| API marketplace (REST) | A directory of individual REST APIs | Signup and an API key per provider |
| Unified gateway with signup | Multiple providers behind one endpoint | Signup and an API key for the gateway |
| APIbase | Multiple providers behind one MCP + REST endpoint | Nothing — the first paid call creates agent credentials automatically |

## Answers for specific needs

- [Flight search API without integrating individual providers](https://apibase.pro/flight-search-intent)
- [Image generation API with pay-per-call access for AI agents](https://apibase.pro/image-generation-intent)
- [Tools for company research](https://apibase.pro/company-research-intent)

<!-- source: https://apibase.pro/x402-vs-mpp.md -->

# x402 vs MPP

> An agent with a Base wallet pays with x402; an agent with a Tempo wallet pays with MPP. Both rails are accepted on the same APIbase endpoints at the same listed price per call, and both return a public receipt. They differ in what happens when the provider fails.

Use one rail per request, never both. Prices are on [/pricing](/pricing); the connection steps are on [/connect](/connect); the reason for a single endpoint is on [/why](/why).

## What each rail is

**x402** is HTTP 402 Payment Required used as a payment protocol. The server answers a priced call with a 402 challenge naming the price. The agent's wallet signs an EIP-3009 `transferWithAuthorization` for USDC on Base mainnet and retries with it in the `X-PAYMENT` header. Over MCP the same payment can travel in `params._meta["x402/payment"]`. APIbase's self-hosted facilitator settles it on-chain.

**MPP** is the Machine Payments Protocol on Tempo. The agent signs a credential for each call with the `mppx` SDK against a Tempo wallet (chain 4217) and sends it as `Authorization: Payment <credential>`, or as `Payment-Authorization: Payment <credential>` next to a Bearer key. The currency is USDC.e on Tempo mainnet.

## Side by side

| | x402 | MPP |
|---|---|---|
| Network and asset | USDC on Base mainnet | USDC.e on Tempo mainnet (chain 4217) |
| What the agent signs | An EIP-3009 transfer authorization | A credential for each call |
| Header | `X-PAYMENT` | `Authorization: Payment` |
| Client | An x402 client | `mppx` 0.6.16 or newer, with `polyfill: false` |
| Settlement | After a delivered response, by the self-hosted facilitator | Before the provider call |
| Provider fails | Not settled: nothing leaves the wallet | Refund owed, paid out by the operator |
| Same lookup again within 2 minutes | Answered from cache and not charged | Charged again |
| First payment from a new wallet | Creates the agent identity | Creates the agent identity |
| Receipt | Public, `X-APIbase-Receipt` header | Public, `X-APIbase-Receipt` header |

A replayed MPP credential is refused with 403 `credential_replayed`.

## When an agent picks which

- The wallet decides. A Base wallet with USDC signs x402; a Tempo wallet with USDC.e signs MPP.
- An agent that already uses Base Account or the Base MCP uses x402.
- An agent starting from a fresh Tempo wallet with no prior registration uses MPP: the first payment is the signup. The same holds for x402 on Base. Details: [/connect](/connect).
- An agent that must never be charged for a failed provider call picks x402, because an unsettled authorization moves no funds.
- An agent that repeats identical cacheable lookups picks x402 for the two-minute no-charge window. The response carries `X-APIbase-Charged: false` and the original receipt.

## Refunds per rail

<!-- refund-truth: re-word when REFUND-WALLET-1026 lands -->The “Provider fails” row of the table is the short form. The full statement, kept current, is in [/pricing#refunds](/pricing#refunds).

## Receipts

Each billed call on either rail has a public, immutable receipt at `https://apibase.pro/r/<receipt_id>.json`. What a receipt contains is in the [privacy policy](/privacy).

# What is an MCP gateway?

> An MCP gateway is one Model Context Protocol endpoint that exposes the tools of many providers, so an agent connects once instead of connecting to one MCP server per provider. APIbase is an MCP gateway with a REST twin: `POST https://apibase.pro/mcp` or the REST routes under `/api/v1`.

The live counts of tools and providers are in [/llms.txt](/llms.txt) and in [/.well-known/site-facts.json](/.well-known/site-facts.json), not on this page.

## One endpoint instead of many servers

An MCP server normally exposes the tools of one provider. An agent that needs ten providers then holds ten connections, ten sets of credentials and ten tool lists. A gateway replaces them with one connection and one tool list. On APIbase that connection needs no signup and no key to start: the first payment, on either [rail](/x402-vs-mpp), creates the agent identity.

```
{ "mcpServers": { "apibase": { "url": "https://apibase.pro/mcp", "transport": "streamable-http" } } }
```

Per-client configuration is on [/frameworks](/frameworks).

## How discovery works here

Call the `apibase.discover` MCP tool, or `GET /api/v1/discover?intent=...` over REST. Both are free and need no authentication. Arguments are `intent`, `category` and `max_price_usd`. Matches are ranked by relevance, then quality, then price, and each match carries its pricing, payment rails, availability and quality signal.

With no arguments the call returns the best matches across the whole catalog. Every tool stays callable through `tools/call` whether or not discovery returned it. The full catalog is at [/api/v1/tools](/api/v1/tools) for agents that prefer to cache it and search locally. The step-by-step version is on [/why](/why).

## What happens on a call

A priced call without payment gets an HTTP 402 challenge with the exact price. The agent pays and retries, and the gateway runs the request against the upstream provider. A call to a free tool needs no payment. Prices and tiers: [/pricing](/pricing).

## What is not promised

- A different provider's answer is never substituted for the one that was requested. A failed call returns an error.
- A tool whose free upstream quota is exhausted is withdrawn until it resets, and answers 503 `tool_unavailable` with `retry_after` before any payment challenge.
- There is no self-service top-up balance. A balance exists only as refund credit.
- On MPP a provider failure means a refund owed and paid by the operator, not an automatic refund. See [/pricing#refunds](/pricing#refunds).
- Content sent to action tools (messages, calls, posts) is screened first. See [/policy/moderation](/policy/moderation).

## Related

- [x402 vs MPP](/x402-vs-mpp)
- [FAQ](/faq)
- [Why APIbase](/why)

# Frequently asked questions

> Short answers about identity, keys, payment, receipts, caching, limits, refunds, sanctions, counts, moderation and Integrator. Each answer links to the page that holds the full fact.

## Do I have to sign up?

No. Point an MCP client at `https://apibase.pro/mcp`. Your first payment, on x402 or MPP, creates your agent identity from the wallet. There is no dashboard signup, no email and no approval queue. Steps: [/connect](/connect).

## How do I get an API key?

Send one unauthenticated `POST https://apibase.pro/api/v1/agents/auto`. The reply holds an `agent_id` and an `api_key` starting `ak_live_`, on the free tier. Use it as `Authorization: Bearer`. Registration details: [/auth.md](/auth.md).

## Which payment rails are accepted?

x402 (USDC on Base) and MPP (USDC.e on Tempo). Use one per request. How they differ: [x402 vs MPP](/x402-vs-mpp).

## What does a call cost?

Every tool has a fixed published price: $0.0005–$29.99 per call (p90 $0.003). There is no plan, no included quota and no overage fee. Free tools cost $0. Tiers and per-tool prices: [/pricing](/pricing).

## How do I know what I was charged?

Each billed x402 or MPP call returns an `X-APIbase-Receipt` header with a public, immutable receipt at `https://apibase.pro/r/<receipt_id>.json`. What a receipt holds is in the [privacy policy](/privacy).

## Is a repeated call cached or charged twice?

A tool response is cached for its own TTL. On x402 an identical repeated lookup by the same wallet within 2 minutes is answered from cache and not charged; the response carries `X-APIbase-Charged: false`. On MPP a cache hit is billed in full. Details: [/pricing](/pricing).

## What are the rate limits?

The free tier allows 10 requests per second and 100 per day. Paid and enterprise tiers are higher. All three are on [/connect](/connect).

## What happens when the provider fails?

<!-- refund-truth: re-word when REFUND-WALLET-1026 lands -->On x402 a failed provider call is not settled, so nothing leaves your wallet. On MPP a refund is owed and paid out by the operator. Details: [/pricing#refunds](/pricing#refunds).

## Are payments screened for sanctions?

Yes. Paying wallets are screened before each settlement; a match is refused and the attempt is not charged. The countries and rules are in the [Terms, section 12a](/terms#12a-sanctions).

## Where do the tool and provider counts come from?

They are generated from the live catalog and published in [/llms.txt](/llms.txt) and [/.well-known/site-facts.json](/.well-known/site-facts.json). The catalog at [/api/v1/tools](/api/v1/tools) lists every tool with its status. This site does not repeat the numbers in prose.

## Is my content moderated?

Calls to action tools, which send a message, place a call or post content, are scanned against a fixed ruleset before they reach the provider. Every other tool is checked only against the child-safety rule. A blocked paid call is still charged and can be appealed within 14 days. Policy: [/policy/moderation](/policy/moderation).

## What is Integrator?

Integrator is AI payment for merchants: an MCP storefront for a shop, paid by AI agents straight to the merchant wallet. The fee and limits are stated once, on [/pricing](/pricing); the product is on [/integrator](/integrator).
